tagline: Out of Clintwood, past places that explain their names.
intro: Brush Creek Road leaves Clintwood, the Dickenson County seat, and hands off to Route 611, which goes by the names South of the Mountain, Blowing Rock and Bartlick roads. Between them they reach Isom, Blowing Rock and Bartlick and end at Route 80 near Haysi. Clintwood itself began in 1829 as Holly Creek, after the stream through town.
The names along the way come with their reasons attached. Isom is named for Isom Mullins, a pioneer, and Blowing Rock for a rock that blows debris about when the wind is up.

moments.title: Clintwood
moments.text: In 1948 the town elected an all-female council, nicknamed the Petticoat Government, which organized a fire department, bought a fire truck and drew the interest of Lady Astor.

moments.title: Skeetrock
moments.text: Skeetrock took its name from locals who would skate, or skeet, on the slippery creek bed, and it kept a post office from 1901 to 1958.

moments.title: Bartlick
moments.text: Near the end of the road, Bartlick joins the name of a resident, Bartley Belcher, to the salt licks found round about.
